definitions.gloss: at once, immediately, right away, promptly
definitions.explanation: Indicates that an action is taken without delay, often in response to something.

examples.japanese: {早速|さっそく}{始|はじ}めましょう。
メールを{受|う}け{取|と}って{早速|さっそく}{返事|へんじ}した。
examples.english: I received the email and replied immediately.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいレシピを{早速|さっそく}{試|ため}してみた。
examples.english: I tried out the new recipe right away.

notes:
{早速|さっそく} conveys acting promptly in response to something — you heard about it, so you did it right away. It implies eagerness or willingness, not urgency.

POSITION:
Typically appears at the beginning of a sentence or directly before the verb.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {早速|さっそく}ですが…: Getting right to the point… (polite conversation opener)
- {早速|さっそく}{試|ため}す: to try right away
- {早速|さっそく}{始|はじ}める: to start right away

SIMILAR WORDS:
- すぐに: immediately, at once (neutral — no nuance of eagerness)
- {直|ただ}ちに: immediately (formal, often implies urgency)
- {即座|そくざ}に: instantly (formal, very fast response)

REGISTER:
Usable in both casual and polite speech. {早速|さっそく}ですが is a standard way to transition to the main topic in business meetings and formal emails.
